title: Streamline configuration
description: Schema for a Streamline config file. Mirrors internal/config Config struct, validator tags and defaults(). All keys are optional — unset keys fall back to built-in defaults; `streamline config init` emits every key with its default.

logRotate.description: Size/age based log rotation (applies when output is a file path).

replace_whole_season.description: Take a season pack whole when it beats the season's best file, instead of replacing only the episodes it outscores. Off by default.

allowed_codecs.description: ffprobe video codec names ("hevc", "av1", "h264"). A grab whose probed codec isn't in this list is held. Empty means any codec.

formats.description: Scored formats evaluated against a candidate release. Each name must resolve to either a built-in format or an entry in custom_formats.

score.description: May be negative, to penalize a matched format.

min_score.description: Minimum total matched-format score a release must reach to be accepted.

upgrade_until_score.description: Stops upgrade-seeking once the current score reaches this value. 0 means no cap.

type.description: Condition kind. release_title/release_group match pattern as a regex against the release title/group. resolution/source/codec match value case-insensitively (resolution accepts 720p/1080p/2160p only). size checks the release size against min_gb/max_gb. seeders checks the seeder count against min.

pattern.description: Regex pattern. Required for release_title and release_group.

value.description: Exact match value. Required for resolution, source and codec.

required.description: When true, this condition must pass for the format to match. When false (the default), it joins the optional group: at least one optional condition must pass for the format to match.

name.description: Must not collide with a built-in format name (see internal/quality Builtins()).

description.description: Optional free-text explanation of what the format detects, shown alongside the format in the UI.

data_dir.description: Directory holding runtime data. Created at boot if missing.

read_only.description: Reject all runtime config write-backs (config.Update). For declarative/GitOps deploys where config is mounted read-only; changes flow through git, not the UI.

torrent_listen_port.description: Overrides the builtin download client's listen_port. Top-level so STREAMLINE_TORRENT_LISTEN_PORT can reach it — nothing inside download_clients[] is addressable from the environment. Intended for a VPN that assigns a forwarded port per session, which rotates and so cannot be written into a git-owned config file.

trusted_proxies.description: CIDR ranges of reverse proxies allowed to set X-Forwarded-* headers. Empty trusts none, so the connecting peer is always treated as the client. WARNING: list the proxies themselves, as narrowly as possible (ideally /32 or /128 each) — never a whole client subnet. Naming a range clients can also occupy (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, a Kubernetes pod or node CIDR) makes every host in it a trusted proxy: any of them can then forge X-Forwarded-For to claim an address inside auth.trusted_networks and be granted auth.trusted_role without authenticating.

session_secret.description: JWT HMAC signing secret. Auto-generated and persisted on first boot when empty.

session_secret_file.description: Path to a file holding session_secret. Mutually exclusive with session_secret.

seed_admin.description: Optional bootstrap admin, applied only against an empty database. An empty email resolves to admin@streamline.local and, when no password and no password_file are configured, that account gets a generated password printed once to stdout.

role_claim.description: ID-token claim (e.g. "groups") used for role mapping. Accepts a dotted path into nested claims, e.g. "realm_access.roles" for Keycloak.

role_mapping.description: Maps a role_claim value to a Streamline role. Highest-privilege match wins, capped by the provider's allow_admin ceiling; authoritative when set, except on the login that adopts an existing local account by email, which never changes the role.

email_linking.description: Whether a federated identity this provider has never presented before may sign in as an existing account because the email addresses match. Default disabled: the provider's email claim is not proof of account ownership, so it adopts nothing. non_admin is the migration setting — it adopts non-admin accounts, so turn it on, have everyone sign in once to bind their identities, then turn it back off. all adopts any account, admin included. It gates the adoption, not its result: a login matching an identity an adoption already linked never reads this key, so setting it back to disabled keeps every account adopted while it was open reachable. Governs adoption only; roles are allow_admin's business.

allow_admin.description: Whether this provider may put an account on the admin role. Default false, in which case no role it confers is ever admin — not the claim-mapped role, not the auth.oidc_default_role a provisioning login falls back to, and not the role carried by an invite consumed through SSO. Independent of email_linking, so no change to either setting can raise capability on the other axis.

download_path.description: Host-side directory streamline reads completed torrents from. Combined with the torrent name to locate content (<download_path>/<torrent.Name>).

monitor_specials.description: Monitor season 0 (specials) when a series is added or a refresh discovers the season. Off by default.

drift_grace_ticks.description: Consecutive drift_check ticks a MediaFile may be missing before its row is deleted.

always_ask.description: Hold every import for a decision, even when every check passes.

min_duration_ratio.description: Hold an import whose probed duration is less than this share of the known runtime.

schedules.description: Cron-like job intervals (Go duration strings). One key per registered job; media-scoped jobs are keyed movie_*/tv_*, the rest are shared across both libraries.

rss_sync.description: Deprecated: renamed to movie_rss_sync. Still honoured, with a warning on boot.

missing_search.description: Deprecated: split into movie_missing_search and tv_missing_search. Still honoured for both, with a warning on boot.

metadata_refresh.description: Deprecated: split into movie_metadata_refresh and tv_metadata_refresh. Still honoured for both, with a warning on boot.

orphan_scan.description: Deprecated: split into movie_orphan_scan and tv_orphan_scan. Still honoured for both, with a warning on boot.

tmdb_region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 uppercase region code, e.g. "FR".

ffmpeg.description: ffmpeg-suite dependency (ffprobe today, the player's transcoder later).

enabled.description: false makes probing and everything built on it inert.

path.description: Directory holding the ffmpeg/ffprobe binaries. Empty resolves via $PATH.

output.description: "stderr", an absolute file path, or a path relative to data_dir.
"stderr", an absolute file path, or a path relative to data_dir.

endpoint.description: OTLP endpoint. Empty disables OTel export.

plex_client_id.description: X-Plex-Client-Identifier. Auto-generated on first boot when empty.

quality_profiles.description: Named quality profiles. Setting this to an empty list leaves every movie without a resolvable profile, and is not rejected: the check that quality_default_profile names a real profile only runs on a non-empty list.

quality_default_profile.description: Name of the quality profile used when a movie names none. Must name an entry in quality_profiles whenever that list has any.

custom_formats.description: User-defined quality formats, scored per quality profile via quality_profiles[].formats.
